questions.q: What does CREATE USER app_svc FOR LOGIN app_svc actually do?
options: Creates a database-level principal in the current database, mapped to the server login app_svc
Creates a new server login named app_svc
Grants db_owner to the login app_svc
Changes the database's containment level
questions.explain: CREATE USER ... FOR LOGIN creates a database user (database-scoped principal) mapped to an existing server login — it grants no permissions by itself.

options: A database user whose SID no longer matches any server login on the instance
A login that was never granted any permissions
A user that belongs to no fixed database role
A contained database user by definition
questions.explain: Orphaned users commonly occur after restoring a database onto a different instance where the matching server login doesn't exist (or has a different SID).

questions.q: What must be true of a database before you can create a contained database user in it?
options: Its containment level must be set to PARTIAL
It must be in SIMPLE recovery model
Mixed Mode authentication must be disabled instance-wide
It must have at least one fixed server role assigned
questions.explain: Contained users require the database's containment level to be PARTIAL (the only supported containment level today).

questions.q: In sys.database_principals, what does authentication_type_desc = 'DATABASE' indicate?
options: The user is a contained database user, authenticating with a credential stored inside the database itself
The user is mapped to a Windows-authenticated server login
The user has sysadmin rights
The database is in FULL recovery model
questions.explain: DATABASE means the user's credential lives inside the database (a contained user); INSTANCE means it's backed by a server login.

questions.q: You drop a server login without first dropping the database user mapped to it. What happens to that database user?
options: It becomes orphaned — it still exists but its SID matches no server login
It is automatically dropped along with the login
It automatically converts to a contained user
SQL Server refuses to drop the login while a mapped user exists
questions.explain: SQL Server does not cascade-delete database users when a login is dropped; the user remains but becomes orphaned until re-linked or dropped.
